title: Marche: Gasolio Snaps Back While Metano's Ten-Week Climb Keeps Outrunning the Rest of Italy
dek: A sharp one-day pullback in diesel prices masks the bigger story in Marche: methane has climbed nearly 23% since tracking began, and LPG keeps sitting stubbornly a fifth above the national average.
executive_summary: As of September 29, 2026, self-service Benzina in Marche stands at €2.1072/L and Gasolio at €2.3206/L, both running about 1.3% below their national same-day averages (€2.1351 and €2.3498 respectively). GPL is flat at €0.899/L and Metano flat at €1.7908/L, both unchanged from the prior reading. The day's biggest single-day move was Gasolio, which fell 2.51% from €2.3803 just two days earlier — the sharpest daily drop of any fuel in the region right now, pulling it back from what had been the highest weekly average recorded since tracking began on July 21.

Zoom out to the ten weeks of history in the tracker, though, and a different fuel stands out: Metano. Marche's self-service methane price has risen from €1.4581/L in the week of July 20 to €1.7908/L in the week of September 21 — a 22.82% climb, outpacing the 19.33% national increase over the same stretch and making it both the fastest-moving fuel tracked in the region and the one with the widest region-versus-nation gap in percentage terms. GPL tells a quieter but equally notable story: Marche's LPG price has nudged up 1.12% over the same weeks while the national average actually eased 0.49%, leaving Marche's GPL sitting roughly 19% above the rest of the country — by far the largest structural premium of any fuel in today's data.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Eases in Step With the Rest of the Country
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Marche closed at €2.1072/L on September 29, down 2.01% from €2.1505/L on September 27 (served: €2.2771/L, versus €2.3165/L). That puts the region 1.31% below the national self-service average of €2.1351/L for the same day — a modest but consistent discount that has held through the recent run-up in prices.

Over the ten weeks tracked, Marche's Benzina has risen from a €1.9544/L weekly average in the week of July 20 to €2.1473/L in the week of September 21 — a 9.87% increase, tracking almost exactly with the national move of 9.68% over the same period. The steepest week-on-week jump came between the weeks of September 7 and September 14 (€2.0657 to €2.1242, +2.83%), mirroring a national acceleration of similar size — Marche is not diverging from the rest of Italy on this fuel, just moving with it.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio's Sharpest Pullback of the Tracked Period
paragraphs: Gasolio posted the single biggest daily move of any fuel in Marche today: self-service fell 2.51%, from €2.3803/L on September 27 to €2.3206/L on September 29 (served: €2.5525/L down to €2.492/L). That leaves the region 1.24% below the national self-service average of €2.3498/L — a discount similar in size to Benzina's.

The bigger picture is a steady multi-week climb followed by a sudden give-back. Marche's weekly Gasolio average rose from €2.1524/L (week of July 20) to €2.3496/L (week of September 21), a 9.16% increase that tracks almost exactly with the national 9.14% gain over the same period. That September 21 week set the highest weekly average recorded in the region since tracking began on July 21 — and today's price sits noticeably below where that peak week left off, the first real sign of Gasolio cooling after two months of steady gains.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL: Marche's Persistent Premium Over the Rest of Italy
paragraphs: GPL held flat at €0.899/L self-service in Marche on both September 27 and September 29 (served ticked up marginally, €0.7832/L to €0.7834/L). What stands out is the gap to the national figure: at €0.7551/L nationally, Marche is running 19.06% above the national self-service average — by a wide margin the largest region-versus-nation gap of any fuel in today's data.

That premium isn't new — it has been a structural feature of the region throughout the tracked period, and it's widening rather than closing. Marche's weekly GPL average edged up from €0.889/L (week of July 20) to €0.899/L (week of September 21), a 1.12% increase, while the national average actually eased over the same stretch, from €0.7592/L to €0.7555/L, a 0.49% decline. Marche and the rest of Italy are moving in opposite directions on this fuel.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Posts the Region's Biggest Multi-Week Climb
paragraphs: Self-service Metano in Marche held at €1.7908/L on September 29, unchanged from September 27 (served: €1.8785/L versus €1.8795/L) — the price has in fact been flat since September 19, an unusually static stretch for the fuel that has otherwise moved the most of any product tracked. Against the national self-service average of €1.7935/L, Marche is running just 0.15% below, essentially in line with the rest of the country today.

The multi-week trend is where Metano separates itself from every other fuel in this report. Marche's weekly average rose from €1.4581/L (week of July 20) to €1.7908/L (week of September 21) — a 22.82% increase, the largest of any fuel tracked in the region, and comfortably ahead of the 19.33% national increase over the same period. That roughly 3.5-point gap between Marche's climb and the national one is the widest of any fuel in this report, making Metano both the fastest mover and the most regionally divergent fuel in the ten weeks of data collected so far.

network_section.heading: Station Network: Marche Reports at a Higher Rate Than the National Average
paragraphs: Marche has 777 registered stations as of September 29, of which 728 reported a price that day — a 93.69% reporting rate. That compares favorably to the national reporting rate of 90.58% (21,684 of 23,940 registered stations), meaning Marche's daily price averages in this report rest on a slightly more complete picture of the local market than the national figures do.

The registered count has crept up slightly over the tracked period, from 774 stations in late July to 777 today, while daily reporting has fluctuated in a narrow band of roughly 725 to 735 stations throughout. That stability suggests the region's averages have been built on a consistent, comparable sample of stations since tracking began, rather than swinging month to month because stations dropped in or out of the reporting pool.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made
paragraphs: Every figure in this report — the daily prices, the region rotation that picked Marche today, the week-by-week trend analysis, and the prose itself — is produced automatically each morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. The system pulls the day's price and registry data, computes regional and national averages across all four fuel types, rotates deterministically through Italy's 20 regions so every region gets its turn in the spotlight, and then has an AI agent read the resulting numbers and write up what's actually notable in them, with no template filled in by rote and no manual copy-paste.

That stands in contrast to how a report like this would traditionally get built: someone manually downloading a CSV export each morning, pasting it into a spreadsheet, recalculating averages by hand, and writing up the highlights before anyone can act on the numbers. The automated version removes that entire manual step — the same task that used to take a person the better part of an hour now happens unattended before most people have opened their laptop.

closing.heading: Explore the Full Dashboard

From there, use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or another Operator/Brand — including a direct look at Marche's own numbers — to explore how prices compare across the dimension that matters most to you.

pull_quote: Metano in Marche has climbed 22.82% since tracking began in July — outrunning the national 19.33% increase by the widest region-versus-nation gap of any fuel in this report.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight lands on Marche, and the standout story isn't the daily price move — it's what happens when you zoom out. Self-service Metano in the region has climbed 22.82% since tracking began in late July, outpacing the 19.33% national increase over the same ten weeks, the widest gap between a region and the national trend of any fuel we track. GPL tells a quieter version of the same story: Marche sits 19% above the national LPG average, and that gap has been widening, not closing, even as the rest of Italy's GPL prices eased slightly. Meanwhile Gasolio just posted its sharpest single-day pullback of the tracked period, down 2.51% after setting its highest weekly average since the tracker began.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating interactive dashboard and daily report covering fuel prices across every Italian region, province, municipality, and brand, rebuilt from scratch every morning with fresh MIMIT data. Take a look and explore your own region at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/.

What I like about this project is what it replaces: not a person exporting a CSV every morning and rebuilding a spreadsheet by hand, but an unattended pipeline, built with Claude Code, that pulls the data, computes the regional and national trends, rotates through Italy's regions, and writes up what's actually notable — automatically, before most people have opened their laptop. It's a small example of a bigger shift: AI tools like Claude Code make it realistic for one person to build and operate something that used to need a standing manual process.
